_: The future-context scenarios for 70-76 Riley Street: scripts/future_context.ts draws them over the capacity study's data. Properties are named by the start of their address as the NSW property register writes it. A building's `toCentre` keeps it so many metres from the middle of a named road (a straight line halfway between the lots either side); `site.tower.toCentre` holds our own tower the same way. A building's `storeys` may be "parity": it rises until its parcel reaches our density (our building's FSR as the scenario draws it, or `site.fsr` where the file states one), a single tower made shallower from its back to land on it. A building is a footprint type (single: single loaded, 12 m deep; d18: double loaded, 18 m, 8 units a floor; d22: double loaded, up to 22 m, 10 units a floor, east and west facing; block: the whole parcel, apartments on every face that is not a party wall; consent: as approved; podium: the street wall over the whole parcel), its storeys, and the line its long axis follows: `along` a street (`side` north, south, east or west picks the frontage where the street wraps the parcel) or the party wall of a `neighbour`, `setback` metres off that line, `depth` metres deep from it (the type's depth unless smaller), `sides` off each end, `length` at most (45 m whatever is asked), kept `from` a named street's end with `endSetback` off it, or `centre`. `footprint: lot` fills the parcel. Every neighbour's building stands on a podium over its whole lot (the street wall), the slab or tower from `base` up. `neighbourSetback: adg` keeps every slab or tower above its podium half the ADG separation off each neighbouring lot (12 m at nine storeys and over, 9 at five to eight, 6 below); a building's own `boundary` sets other metres. `streetSetback: 3` keeps every slab or tower above its podium at least that far off each street and lane, as our tower keeps 3 m off Riley Street and Crown Lane; a building's own `streetBoundary` sets other metres. Prose may use {A.area}, {A.plate}, {A.fsr}, {A.parity}, {A.gap} and {units}. `site.tower` draws our own scheme as a podium and a tower inset from the lot by the setbacks named per street or neighbour; `site.tower.habitable` says which of its faces carry habitable rooms or balconies. A scenario's own `retained` list overrides the study's. A scenario's own `site.tower` moves our tower for that sheet. This file is the three scenarios of every neighbour at our density: `deck: two-sheet` prints two sheets a scenario, its geometry and its view from the sun, and nothing else. A `plate` is a tower with no unit depth asked of it: the lot less its setbacks (`boundary` off its neighbouring lots, `streetBoundary` off its streets, `streets` naming a street's own figure, `toCentre` a road's middle); `maxStoreys` holds a tower at "parity" to a height, and the table then says what density that reaches. A plate may also take `boundaries` (a neighbouring lot's own figure, by its address), a street's or road's name with `@north`, `@south`, `@east` or `@west` where the street wraps the lot, and `wings`: of the plate only a band so many metres deep along each street named, so two wings make an L; a wing may also run along the boundary with a neighbouring lot, named by its address.

site._fsr: Calculated off the plans of 10 November, gross floor area as the LEP counts it (inside the external walls; lifts, stairs, plant and balconies out). The tower, levels 3 to 13: the enclosed outline 41.6 × 20.5 m less its two slots and two corner cut-outs is 793 m², less lifts, stairs and risers (30 m²) and the external walls' thickness (42 m²), about 720 m² a floor, 7,930 m² over 11 floors. Levels 1 and 2: enclosed 47.5 × 20.5 m less the slots is 932 m², less core and walls about 860 m² a floor, 1,720 m². The ground floor is taken at 60 % of the lot, 840 m², its plan not seen. 10,490 m² over the 1,396 m² site is 7.5:1. The plans' own GFA schedule should replace it.
site.label: our site, SSD proposal

tower._: The SSDA plans as marked up on 10 November 2026 (Fuse Architects, 2613; sheets 105 and 108): the ground floor over the lot; levels 1 and 2 held 3 m off Crown Lane (6 m from its middle), 11 apartments a floor; the tower one footprint from level 3 to the top, 6 m off Crown Lane (9 m from its middle), 3 m off Riley Street, Stanley Lane and 66-68 Riley Street, with a slot cut into each long face where the corridor ends, 8 apartments a floor. `podium` counts the storeys under the tower, the ground floor with them; `podiumSetbacks` holds the podium's upper levels off a street; `steps`, where a tower has them, push it further back from a storey up (storeys counted from the ground floor as 1); `levelZero` names the levels as the plans do, GF then L1. `units` lays the apartments out face by face, east and west from the north end and south from the east end, each as [name, width in metres, corner flag where it also has windows or a balcony on that end wall]; a null name is a stretch without an apartment, and with a third figure a slot that many metres deep cut into the tower there.
